summative_rubric.title: Place Value Detectives — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: End-of-unit rubric covering all 7 expectations B1.1-B1.7. Used to score each child against four levels.

rows.expectation_text: read, represent, compose, and decompose whole numbers up to and including 200, using a variety of tools and strategies, and describe various ways they are used in everyday life

levels.descriptor: Reads numerals to 99 reliably; struggles with 3-digit numbers; confuses 132 vs 312.
Reads numerals to 200 with prompts; builds with correct counts but sometimes wrong placements.
Reads, builds, and decomposes numbers to 200 with at least the standard hundreds-tens-ones split.
Produces multiple flexible decompositions (e.g., 132 = 100+30+2 = 130+2 = 100+20+12); volunteers real-life uses for 3-digit numbers.

rows.expectation_text: compare and order whole numbers up to and including 200, in various contexts

levels.descriptor: Defaults to ones-first or biggest-digit reasoning. Gets cross-hundred comparisons wrong (89 > 102).
Applies hundreds-first rule with prompts. Gets same-hundreds comparisons right but reverts on edge cases.
Independently applies hundreds-first rule. Compares and orders 4+ numbers to 200 correctly including cross-hundred pairs.
Articulates the place-value rule unprompted; orders 5+ numbers including same-hundreds-different-tens close pairs; extends rule to 3+ digit comparisons.

rows.expectation_text: estimate the number of objects in collections of up to 200 and verify their estimates by counting

levels.descriptor: Guesses without strategy; estimates often more than 25 off at scale 200.
Uses chunk-of-10 with prompting; over-uses it for huge collections; estimates within 20% of actual.
Selects chunk-of-10 vs chunk-of-100 based on collection size; estimates within 10% of actual at scale 200.
Uses hybrid strategy (chunk-of-100 for bulk + chunk-of-10 for remainder); estimates within 5% of actual; explains the strategy choice unprompted.

rows.expectation_text: count to 200, including by 20s, 25s, and 50s, using a variety of tools and strategies

levels.descriptor: Counts by 5s and 10s starting from 0; cannot skip-count by 25s or 50s.
Counts by 25s and 50s starting from 0 with prompts; struggles to start from non-multiple.
Counts by 20s, 25s, 50s to 200 starting from 0 or other multiples; uses the 0-200 number line as scaffold.
Skip-counts fluently from any number; volunteers count-back by 25s or 50s; uses skip-counting in real-life contexts.

rows.expectation_text: describe what makes a number even or odd

levels.descriptor: Pairs up small concrete collections; doesn't yet recognise that leftover means odd. Or applies majority-of-digits reasoning ('27 is half-and-half').
Uses pair-up test for collections under 20; applies last-digit rule with prompts on bigger numbers.
Independently applies the last-digit rule for any number to 200. Connects skip-counting by 2s to even numbers.
Articulates WHY only the last digit decides (the tens always pair perfectly; only the ones can have a leftover); extends to 3+ digit numbers; volunteers connections to multiples of 2.

rows.expectation_text: use drawings to represent, solve, and compare the results of fair-share problems that involve sharing up to 10 items among 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 10 sharers

levels.descriptor: Distributes objects unevenly OR stops at 'fair share with leftover' for small numbers; cannot handle 3+ sharers fluently.
Shares evenly when totals divide cleanly; struggles to match the leftover-fraction to the number of sharers.
Shares fairly between 2, 3, 4, or 6 sharers including fractional leftovers (cuts into halves, thirds, sixths to match).
Generalises to 5, 8, 10 sharers; volunteers when a leftover requires multiple cuts; explains why fraction matches sharers.

rows.expectation_text: recognize that one third and two sixths of the same whole are equal, in fair-sharing contexts

levels.descriptor: Recognises thirds and sixths as separate fractions; does not yet see 1/3 = 2/6 even with overlay demo.
Recognises 1/3 = 2/6 after the pizza-overlay demo.
Recognises 1/3 = 2/6 unprompted; applies to a new context (e.g., share scenarios).
Generalises to other equivalences (e.g., 2/3 = 4/6, 1/2 = 3/6); volunteers connections to compose/decompose; sees fraction equivalence as a structural property.

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Apply this rubric to each child's combined evidence: diagnostic tracker (Lesson 1) + L2/L3/L4 formative trackers + summative worksheet (Lesson 5). The level achieved is the LOWEST of the relevant evidence sources for that expectation.

summative_task_script.title: Lesson 5 Summative Task — Fair Shares and Fraction Equivalence
summative_task_script.purpose: End-of-unit summative assessment. Captures evidence for B1.6 (fair-share with 2-10 sharers including fractional leftovers) and B1.7 (1/3 = 2/6 equivalence) explicitly via the worksheet.
administration_steps: Bring children back to the carpet after the small-group rotations on Day 5.
Hold up the worksheet and walk through the four parts: (1) even shares, (2) fractional shares, (3) equivalence prompt, (4) reasoning prompt.
Distribute one worksheet per child. Allow 15 minutes for completion.
Walk around and record per-child evidence on the fair-share + fraction tracker.
Collect worksheets and score against the rubric: 9-10/10 = Level 4; 7-8 = Level 3; 5-6 = Level 2; 0-4 = Level 1.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Part 1 (2 even-share scenes, score out of 4): captures B1.6 baseline. Part 2 (2 fractional-share scenes, score out of 4): captures B1.6 mastery (matching fraction to sharers). Part 3 (equivalence prompt, score out of 1): captures B1.7. Part 4 (reasoning prompt, score out of 1): captures B1.7 mastery. Total score out of 10. Map to summative rubric: 9-10 = Level 4 Exceeding; 7-8 = Level 3 Achieving; 5-6 = Level 2 Developing; 0-4 = Level 1 Beginning.

evidence_per_expectation.B1.1: Lesson 1 diagnostic — child reads/builds 3-digit numbers; Lesson 2 formative — flexible decomposition.
evidence_per_expectation.B1.2: Lesson 2 formative — applies hundreds-first comparison rule.
evidence_per_expectation.B1.3: Lesson 4 formative — selects right chunk strategy and gets within 10% of actual.
evidence_per_expectation.B1.4: Lesson 1 diagnostic — skip-counts by 25s; Lesson 4 reinforcement.
evidence_per_expectation.B1.5: Lesson 3 formative — applies last-digit rule; explains pair-up test.
